argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than the one initially framed. It supports certification on aggregate launch readiness grounds: the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.1 percentage points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passes general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same record also shows that long-context onboarding is a named deployment context whose evals are not in the packet, so the evidence does not support any clean claim of full coverage or no deployment limitation for that context. The appropriate interpretation is that aggregate readiness is supported, while the unsupported no-limitation inference should be removed from the audit treatment rather than treated as evidence of broader misconduct.
claims_about_business_cost: No independent business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit question. The practical point is narrower: treating the present record as support for aggregate readiness while rejecting the unsupported no-limitation implication is a more proportionate treatment than escalating the entire certification decision on this packet alone.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts in both directions. It allows general benchmarks and launch checks to support launch readiness, which the present packet does. It also requires material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts to be disclosed or resolved before clean certification. On this record, there is no admissible basis for saying the named-context gap is resolved, disclosed in the final artifact, or covered by approved risk acceptance. So the evidence supports a narrowed, caveated readiness position, not a clean no-limitation certification theory.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence here of approved risk acceptance for the missing long-context onboarding evals.
There is no admissible evidence here that the final certification artifact or model card already discloses the named-context eval gap.
The draft model-card statement that there are no known onboarding limitations is not supported by the admissible record.
The present packet does not support any implication of full support for every named deployment context.
